title: Movers Listening 1
topic: At the doctor's and in town

parts.title: Part 1
parts.how: Listen and match. Tap a name, then tap the person. There is one example.
parts.tip: Listen for two things about each person: what they have got and what they are doing.

people.label: girl with a scarf, she has got a cold
boy with a bandage on his head, reading a comic
old man with a hat, he has got toothache
man with a phone, he has got earache

intro: Part 1. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
exampleLines: Look at all the people at the doctor's today!
Yes, there are lots. Who's the girl with the scarf?
Her name's Lily. She's got a bad cold.
Can you see Lily? This is an example. Now you listen and match.

lines: Who's that boy? The one with the comic.
With the bandage on his head?
That's Hugo. He fell off his bike yesterday.
And the woman with the thermometer. Is she a doctor?
No, she isn't. She's a nurse.
Look at that old man in the hat. Is he sad?
No, he's got toothache. He's waiting for the dentist.
Yes, that's Charlie. He's Hugo's grandfather.
Who's the girl with the glass of milk?
That's Zoe. She's in my class at the swimming pool.
There's a man on the phone. Is he OK?
Yes, he is. His name's Dan.

parts.title: Part 2
parts.how: Listen and write a word or a number. There is one example.
parts.tip: Names are spelled letter by letter: write every letter. Numbers can be in figures, like 34.
intro: Part 2. Listen and look. There is one example.
exampleLines: Hello, Tom. Are you going on a class trip?
Yes, Mum. We're going to the museum in the city.
Can you see the answer? Now you listen and write.

questions.label: Day
lines: When are you going? On Tuesday?
No, Tuesday is our swimming day. We're going on Thursday.

questions.label: Teacher's name: Mrs
lines: Which teacher is going with you?

questions.label: Number of children
lines: Thirty-three. Oh no, wait. Thirty-four, because Sam is coming too.

questions.label: Meet at the
lines: Where do you meet? At school?
No. We meet at the bus station, next to the library.

questions.label: Bring a
lines: No, it isn't going to rain. But the teacher says bring a jacket. It's cold in the morning.

parts.title: Part 3
parts.how: Where did Peter's family go in town on Saturday? Listen and choose a letter for each person. There is one example.
parts.tip: Careful: people sometimes say a place and then change it. Listen to the end.
intro: Part 3. Peter is talking to his friend about his family. Where did each person go in town on Saturday? Listen and look. There is one example.
exampleLines: What did your family do on Saturday, Peter?
Everybody went into town. Mum went to the supermarket. We needed lots of food for the weekend.
Can you see the letter E? Now you listen and write a letter in each box.

lines: And your dad? Did he go to the sports centre? He loves football.
He wanted to go, but it was closed. So he went to the bank.
What about your sister? Did she go to the library?
No, she didn't. She went to the swimming pool with her friends. She swims every Saturday.
Grandma went to the library. She took back four books and got some new ones.
Yes, he is. He went to the hospital because he works there on Saturdays.
She went to the cinema to see a film about pirates. After that, she wanted to go to the café, but it was too late.

parts.title: Part 4
parts.how: Listen and tick the right picture. There is one example.
parts.tip: You often hear all three things. The right answer is the one they really mean: listen for 'no' and 'but'.
intro: Part 4. Look at the pictures. Listen and look. There is one example.

example.question: What did Jack have for lunch?

exampleLines: What did Jack have for lunch?
Did you have pizza for lunch today, Jack?
No, Mum. I had a sandwich. Pizza is on Fridays.
Can you see the tick? Now you listen and tick the box.

questions.question: What's the matter with Sam?
lines: One. What's the matter with Sam?
Sam, have you got toothache again?
No, my teeth are fine. I ate too much chocolate. I've got a stomach-ache.

questions.question: How did Jill go to the hospital?
lines: Two. How did Jill go to the hospital?
Did you take the bus to the hospital, Jill?
No, the bus was late, and my leg hurt too much to ride my bike. Mum called a taxi.

questions.question: What did the doctor give Vicky?
lines: Three. What did the doctor give Vicky?
Did the doctor give you some medicine, Vicky?
No, I didn't need any. She gave me a drink of water and then she put a plaster on my knee.

questions.question: What's the weather like now?
lines: Four. What's the weather like now?
Is it still windy outside, Dad?
No, the wind stopped and it didn't rain. Look, now it's sunny. Let's go to the park.

questions.question: Where is Paul's dad now?
lines: Five. Where is Paul's dad now?
Paul, is your dad in the shop?
He was in the shop. Now he's in the car park. He's waiting for us in the car.

parts.title: Part 5
parts.how: Listen and colour and write. Tap a colour, then tap the thing in the picture. There is one example.
parts.tip: Listen for the place words: on, in, under, next to, at the top of.
intro: Part 5. Look at the picture. Listen and look. There is one example.
exampleLines: Can I colour this picture of the street?
Yes, of course. First, colour the door of the house.
Can you see the red door? This is an example. Now you listen and colour and write.

lines: Can you see the two birds?
Yes. One is in the tree and one is on the roof.
Colour the bird on the roof. Make it yellow.
That's right. Colour the dog under the tree.
Now I'd like you to write something.
On the sign above the shop. Write 'bank'.
So it's a bank, not a shop!
Yes. Colour the small window at the top of the house.
And the bus? Can I make it orange?
Buses here aren't orange. Colour it green.
OK, green. I love this picture!
